name: Bybit cold-wallet theft
loss_note: 401,347 ETH (plus other tokens), reported as $1.4 to $1.5 billion; the FBI says about $1.5 billion.
summary: During a routine transfer from its Ethereum multisig cold wallet to its hot wallet, Bybit signed a transaction that had been changed to hand control of the wallet to the attacker, who then swept about 401,000 ETH. The root cause reported by the forensic firms is malicious code on the Safe{Wallet} interface Bybit signers used. The FBI attributed it to North Korea (TraderTraitor) on 26 Feb 2025. The money was stolen and laundered on Ethereum and other chains; no NEAR Intents activity has been found.
root_cause: Reported by DFNS and others: a malicious contract replaced the logic of Bybit's Safe{Wallet} proxy during a signed transfer; the forensic reports (Sygnia, Verichains, via the press) trace it to malicious JavaScript on Safe{Wallet}'s interface. Not verified here.

attribution.says: North Korea is responsible; the activity is referred to as TraderTraitor (Alert I-022625-PSA, 26 Feb 2025).

notes: The FBI list holds 51 Ethereum addresses it says hold or have held assets from the theft and are operated by or closely connected to TraderTraitor actors; each is recorded as a wallet that held or moved the stolen money. The money was moved on to many more addresses, which are not listed here.

sources.publisher: FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (PSA I-022625-PSA, 26 Feb 2025)
sources.says: About $1.5 billion in virtual assets was stolen from Bybit on or about 21 Feb 2025; North Korea ("TraderTraitor") is responsible; lists 51 Ethereum addresses connected to the theft.

Bybit's cold wallet (a Safe{Wallet} proxy) 0x1Db92e2EeBC8E0c075a02BeA49a2935BcD2dFCF4 held 401,000 ETH; the attacker address 0x47666fab8bd0ac7003bce3f5c3585383f09486e2 received the drained funds through a sweepETH call; two malicious contracts 0x96221423681A6d52E184D440a8eFCEbB105C7242 and 0xbDd077f651EBe7f7b3cE16fe5F2b025BE2969516.
The theft transaction was at 14:16:11 UTC on 21 Feb 2025, 401,347 ETH; the malicious contract 0xbdd077f651ebe7f7b3ce16fe5f2b025be2969516 holds sweepETH and sweepERC20.
Searched by wallet address for the attacker address and the 51 FBI addresses.

intents.checked: On 2026-11-17 the NEAR Intents explorer (wallet or deposit address search) was searched for the 51 FBI addresses, the attacker address 0x47666fab8bd0ac7003bce3f5c3585383f09486e2 and one more address SlowMist reports (0x0fa09C3A328792253f8dee7116848723b72a6d2e, not recorded here): no order was found for any of the 53. Search results were checked against a known sender first. This does not rule out Intents use by other Bybit-linked addresses (the later laundering went to many more); the reported routes are THORChain, eXch and DeFi protocols, not NEAR Intents.
